name: Nuoc mot
summary: A lightly sweet herb drink, cold after a hot walk or hot in the wet months, usually carried away in the hand. The herbs vary by maker: monk fruit and licorice with ginger, lemongrass, cinnamon, lemon, green tea, and chamomile, or with chrysanthemum and lotus leaf.
origin: Hoi An. Vietnam Tourism’s must-try article names it nước mót. The Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 4 December 2025 article names it trà Mót.
taste: Vietnam Tourism steeps ginger, lemongrass, cinnamon, licorice, lemon, green tea, chamomile, and monk fruit.
The 4 December 2025 article steeps monk fruit, licorice, chrysanthemum, and lotus leaf, and calls the cup lightly sweet. Do not merge the lists.
howToEat: Vietnam Tourism says a cold cup after a hot walk, or a hot cup in the wet months, usually taken away.
where: The old town, in the hand.
seoTitle: Nuoc mot — Hoi An herb drink
seoDescription: Nước mót is Hoi An’s herb drink, cold or hot. Vietnam Tourism and a December 2025 article print different herbs.
